props.title: Carrie

sections.content: Carrie revolutionized both horror and coming-of-age films through Brian De Palma's masterful direction of Stephen King's debut novel. The film's unforgettable prom sequence, with its split-screen chaos and operatic violence, influenced countless horror films like A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984) and The Craft (1996). Sissy Spacek's vulnerable yet terrifying performance as Carrie White created the template for sympathetic horror protagonists, while Piper Laurie's portrayal of Margaret White established a new benchmark for psychological horror through religious fanaticism.

sections.content: De Palma's visual style in Carrie heavily influenced modern horror's approach to supernatural phenomena. The film's use of slow motion, split screens, and extreme close-ups during Carrie's telekinetic episodes created a template for depicting psychic powers that echoes through films like Chronicle (2012) and Scanners (1981). The school shower scene's dreamy, almost balletic opening transforms into nightmare, establishing the film's crucial theme of female sexuality as both power and curse.

The film's exploration of religious fundamentalism and maternal abuse broke new ground for horror, paving the way for films like The Witch (2015) and Hereditary (2018). Margaret White's terrifying biblical proclamations and domestic torture created a new archetype of parental horror that influenced everything from Mommie Dearest (1981) to The Babadook (2014). sections.content: Carrie's (1976) influence extends beyond horror into modern examinations of bullying and teenage alienation. Films like Let the Right One In (2008) and Raw (2016) draw from its portrayal of outsider rage and supernatural awakening. The iconic blood-soaked prom scene continues to be referenced and homaged, from Evil Dead (2013) to Ready or Not (2019), cementing its place in horror's visual language.
